title: Instagram comments on Nate Soares's reel "We stop AI. You help?"
artefact_title: Nate Soares (@nateasoares) - "We stop AI. You help?"
central_claim: AI poses a serious existential danger to humanity, and this is worth taking seriously and acting on.
capture_method: Page-text capture of the comment section, pasted into a workbook (no like counts included in this method, unlike the original capture). Threading was not captured either; parent_id and depth are present in comments.csv for shape consistency with the other studies in this series but are blank on every row. Second capture; the first (29 August, via a logged-in browser session against Instagram's own comment API, 1,666 of 1,703 comments with like counts) underpins the published article.

spot_check.note: Random 40-comment sample checked against the codebook on stance, frame, format reaction and emotion; 40/40 agreed, no corrections.

coders: Claude (claude-sonnet-5), twelve parallel coders of about 156 comments each

changelog.note: Logged-in API capture, 1,666 of 1,703 comments, coded with like counts available. Article published from it.

Page-text recapture (2,136 of 2,715 comments then live; likely under-counts unexpanded reply threads, the same limitation seen in the METR Reddit capture) recoded against an 18-frame list. No like counts available in this capture, so engagement-weighted findings from v1 cannot be reproduced or updated. Supersedes v1 for stance/frame shares only.

licence: CC BY 4.0 (coding and compilation; comment text remains its authors')
notes: Unlike the other three studies in this series, this recode has no engagement (like-count) data at all, so like-weighted findings from the original article stand uncorrected pending a future capture that can reach Instagram's comment API. 'other' and off-topic political tangents carry a meaningful share of comments, consistent with the original note's observation that comment threads run wide of the topic.
